text: A traditional spring celebration for the Maidu was the Bear Dance when the Maidu honored the bear coming out of hibernation. The bear's hibernation and survival through the winter symbolized perseverance to the Maidu, who identified with the animal spiritually.

title: Maidu Indians of Northern California - Legends of America
text: Each Maidu band resided in one of three habitats — the inland valleys, the Sierra Nevada foothills, or the mountains. The valley people were prosperous, but poverty was more common in the higher elevations.

title: Mountain Maidu - Drumhop
text: Maidu singers generally use a relaxed and nonpulsating vocal technique. And, compared with Native American songs from other musical areas, they sing large amounts of music with an unchanging beat and with a simple rhythmic organization. The music also has characteristic sequences and syncopations.

title: Maidu | Social Sciences and Humanities | EBSCO Research
text: The Maidu are Indigenous Americans primarily located in northeastern California, with a rich cultural heritage and a legacy of subsistence living through hunting, gathering, and fishing. Traditionally, Maidu people collected acorns, nuts, and berries, using grinding stones for food preparation.
